title: Pharmacist-led intervention to improve LDL-cholesterol control in patients treated with oral lipid lowering agents
summary: The PHARM-LDL study aims, for the first time in Germany, to investigate whether the tested intervention—measuring LDL cholesterol from a finger-prick blood sample in the pharmacy—can improve LDL cholesterol reduction in patients who have been prescribed medication for high cholesterol.
conditions: Disorders of lipoprotein metabolism and other lipidaemias

interventions.name: For patients with a repeat prescription for an oral lipid-lowering agent, current medication adherence is assessed via self-report in the study pharmacy (including the 15-STARS questionnaire). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Written informed consent
- Repeat prescription of an oral lipid-lowering agent: statin monotherapy, ezetimibe monotherapy, bempedoic acid monotherapy, statin/ezetimibe (fixed) combination, bempedoic acid/ezetimibe fixed combination, or other statin fixed combinations
- Potential for optimization of adherence based on 15-STARS/self-report
Exclusion criteria:
Subcutaneous therapy with a lipid-lowering agent (PCSK9 inhibitor; inclisiran).
